correctness.rationale: Borwein–Fabian Thm4 gives a single-defective-line Gâteaux-smooth equivalent norm q. Rotating q via Hilbert isometries gives q_j with uniform bounds m||x||≤q_j(x)≤M||x|| and prescribed exceptional lines; P=Σw_j q_j is a norm and Gâteaux smooth because derivative series uniformly bounded by M. Bregman remainders R_j(x,h)=q_j(x+h)−q_j(x)−Dq_j(x)h≥0 and ≤2M||h|| show exact union of non-Fréchet loci: any bad summand persists, and if all are good dominated tail convergence makes P good. Finite-head norms Q_N=Σ_{j≤N}w_jq_j+2^(-N)||·||_2 have finite bad locus, hereditary MIP via Bandyopadhyay–Gothwal Thm6, and uniform norm/derivative gap ≤(M+1)2^(-N). On every closed Y dim≥2, dense Fréchet support functionals for Q_N|Y approximate any P|Y dual unit functional; continuity at a Q_N smooth support point and Baire avoidance of countably many lines choose z where P is Fréchet smooth; derivative uniform control transfers density, implying MIP via BG Thm2(a). One-dimensional subspaces trivially have MIP. Radial normalization is a sphere homeomorphism, hence a countably dense prescribed direction set remains dense on P-sphere. This is an infinite analytic proof, not extrapolation from finite N.
residual_risks: Implicit use of continuity of the derivative at Fréchet-differentiability points of convex norms is standard and crucial; not a mere pointwise gradient estimate.

value.rationale: Directly resolves an explicit finite-cardinality and infinite-exception problem in hereditary MIP renorming. The countably dense example shows exceptional sets can be topologically large despite hereditary intersection regularity; uniform derivative-transfer is a nontrivial structural result beyond a textbook direct sum.
residual_risks: Restricted to separable real Hilbert space and prescribed countable sets; no arbitrary Banach-space or uncountable-set claim.

final_claim: Every finite or countable family of distinct unoriented directions in separable real infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is exactly the non-Fréchet differentiability directions of an equivalent Gâteaux-smooth norm with hereditary Mazur intersection property, including a countably dense exception set.
limitations: No numerical evidence substitutes for the countably infinite Baire and uniform-dual-approximation arguments.
